comments.author: @mikecane
comments.text: Google's unforgivable mistake is their mishandling of Google Books. They've scanned libraries from all over. It's perhaps the greatest collection of knowledge ever. But they went cheap on OCR. Most OCR is polluted with errors to the point of being unreadable. Had they done in correctly, all of it could have been ingested into their AI and they'd be unbeatable. An instance of Fail Fast, Fail,Forever.

comments.author: @datasciyinfo5133
comments.text: Thanks for this review. I didn't realize Palm2 was so much worse with code. I liked the export to Google docs/sheets feature to export formatted code instead of unformatted code.  Re performance, I am guessing there must be a difference in training data and methods.  Also GPT4 got a big boost when a preview version was released to the public in Nov 2022 (when 3.5 was the main public model and 4 was still being developed.  Lots of human feedback helped OpenAI & Bing improve the March 2023 version (currently available). I already see differences between Bing version of ChatGPT4 and OpenAI version, so the human-feedback difference could be huge.  (I think Bing is censoring itself a lot more in April/May than in early March.  OpenAI is better for code than Bing now.  So there seems to be noticeable drift between these two AI models too.)

comments.author: @nulled7888
comments.text:
Good analysis. Very detailed and skilled editing as well. But please link your sources in the description next time, would be appreciated :)

Personal opinion / prediction on how this will play out:
Open AI had a head start because Google failed to realize the potential of transformers early on in constrast to Open AI. Microsoft is leeching off Open AI now which gives them (in theory at least) the necessary resources to beat Google for now. HOWEVER, as we have seen, the insane amount of public attention AI is getting now makes it very likely that the largest optimizations will come from neither google nor open ai, but instead from individuals. There is no company in the world that could beat the coordinated collective of humanity. That being said, Open Source it is.
